purpose: Resolve the distinction between off-camera deactivation, same-level region scans, and full level reload reconstruction for a normal enemy.

decompile_targets.01F7:1CDA: streams newly visible 64-pixel regions and calls the ARE declaration walker
decompile_targets.01F7:1E04: walks six-byte ARE records, skips records with claim byte 1, marks a new record claimed, invokes the type factory, stores the source record pointer at object+0x1A, and adds the region origin to the local coordinates
decompile_targets.01F7:1DEE: clears object+0x18 and writes zero to the source ARE record claim byte at FS:[object+0x1A+1]

same_level_camera_sweep.interpretation: Clearing the object and ARE claim is not sufficient to make an already-loaded region immediately instantiate the record again; the controlled camera/cache sweep repeatedly entered 1CDA but did not revisit the target at 1E04.

level_reload.interpretation: Level selection rereads the ARE resource and reconstructs the previously deactivated enemy from the same runtime record.

conclusions: Normal enemy off-camera removal is a deactivation plus source-record claim reset, not a permanent death state.
The loaded-region camera sweep did not itself reinstantiate the target record, so an engine should not blindly respawn every cleared object on every visibility pass.
A native level reload rereads the ARE data and recreates the enemy with its original type-specific initializer and steady callback.
The remaining authored question is which region/resource unload transitions, if any, cause the same reconstruction outside a full level reload.
